Article Title: Indian sailor among 5 crew killed by pirates aboard hijacked tanker off Somalia
Article Text:
Vessel was hijacked in April

Five crew members, including an Indian sailor, were killed by Somali pirates aboard a fuel tanker that was hijacked months ago off the coast of Somalia.Security forces have now regained control of the vessel.According to the Puntland Maritime Police Force (PMPF), the victims also included three Pakistani nationals and one Myanmar national."PMPF carried out a maritime operation off the coast of Dharin-baar, Bandar Beyla District, successfully rescuing the MT Honour 25 oil tanker, which had been hijacked by pirates," it said in a social media post on Tuesday.Puntland is a semi-autonomous region of Somalia.According to the PMPF, the pirates had initially offered to surrender while concealing the deaths of the crew members. It further stated that the ship was now safe and under Puntland government control. Sixteen suspected pirates were apprehended during the operation, while efforts to locate the remaining hijackers were continuing.According to the European Union’s naval force Eunavfor, the MT Honour 25 oil tanker was hijacked in April while sailing towards Somalia’s capital, Mogadishu. It was carrying around 17 crew members, most of them Pakistani nationals, along with a cargo of oil products.BBC Somali reported that the crew comprised 10 Pakistanis, four Indonesians, one Indian, one Sri Lankan and one Myanmar national.The commercial vessel, carrying 18,500 barrels of fuel bound for Mogadishu was hijacked on April 21.In a separate development, Somali pirates on Tuesday released a Togo-flagged tanker after holding it off Puntland’s Karkaar region.Nearly 30 armed pirates disembarked from the vessel and handed over all 12 crew members—eight Egyptians and four Indians—unharmed to the local community. The pirates reportedly damaged the vessel, MT Eureka, and set parts of it on fire before fleeing.The tanker had been hijacked on May 2 off Yemen’s Port of Qana while carrying 20,400 barrels of fuel. A substantial amount of its cargo was siphoned off and sold at sea during the months it was held captive. The crew members are now in the care of local residents in the Hul-Aanood area.
Article Summary: Vessel was hijacked in april while sailing towards somalia’s capital, mogadishu. Crew comprised 10 pakistanis, four indonesians, one indian, one sri lankan and one myanmar national. In a separate development, somali pirates on tuesday released a togo-flagged tanker.

NEW DELHI: A key suspect in the 2025 Pahalgam terror attack was killed in Jammu and Kashmir ’s Budgam district, with security forces recovering the body of Pakistan-based Lashkar-e-Taiba ( LeT ) terrorist Mohammad Asif alias Hashim Moosa on Wednesday. The recovery was made along with war-like stores, the security forces said.Moosa, who was among the key suspects in the 2025 Pahalgam terror attack, was found along with war-like stores, as cited by ANI.The Army and other security agencies on Wednesday launched Operation KORAG in the Yousmarg area based on specific intelligence inputs. A joint search operation was initiated after vigilant troops observed suspicious activity and, when challenged, the terrorists opened fire, triggering a fierce exchange of gunfire in which Hashim Moosa was neutralised.According to an update issued by the security forces, the operation remained underway, with personnel continuing search operations in the area.The Srinagar-based Chinar Corps confirmed his death, saying, “During the search early morning in General Area Palmaidan, body of Pak based Lashkar-e-Taiba ( LeT) terrorist, identified as Mohammad Asif alias Hashim Moosa recovered along with war like stores.”Hashim Moosa was among the key suspects named in connection with the 2025 Pahalgam terror attack, which killed 26 tourists.Following the attack, the Jammu and Kashmir Police announced a reward of Rs 20 lakh for information leading to the arrest of Pakistan nationals and LeT terrorists Adil Hussain Thoker, Ali Bhai and Hashim Musa. Security agency sources said Moosa had previously served as a para-commando in Pakistan’s Special Service Group.The National Investigation Agency (NIA) had earlier chargesheeted seven accused in the Pahalgam terror attack case, including Pakistan-based Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) and its alias, The Resistance Front (TRF), both proscribed terrorist organisations. In its 1,597-page chargesheet, the NIA detailed Pakistan’s alleged role in the conspiracy and accused the banned LeT/TRF of planning, facilitating and executing the attack. Pakistani handler and terrorist Sajid Jatt was also named as an accused.
Article Summary: Hasim moosa killed in an encounter in jammu and kashmir’s budgam district. The recovery was made along with war-like stores, the security forces said. Moosa was among the key suspects in the 2025 pahalgam terror attack.

Article Title: As US cozies up to Pakistan, India warns it could impact ties
Article Text:
India and the US had in Feb announced the finalisation of the framework for the first phase of the bilateral trade agreement. However, changes in the US tariff landscape have led to further negotiations on the agreement.

S Jaishankar: Delay in reaching trade deal created bumps in relationship

NEW YORK/ NEW DELHI: Amid growing US-Pakistan bonhomie, external affairs minister S Jaishankar warned that a lack of understanding about India’s concerns over cross-border terrorism will affect India-US bilateral ties.Flagging issues pertaining to each other’s sensitivities, the minister said that terrorism was of particular importance to India.“There are very few countries which have been subjected to the kind of terrorism that we have from a neighbour as part of a deliberate, conscious policy over many, many decades,” Jaishankar said, without naming Pakistan.“Now, if something which matters so deeply to us, there isn’t enough understanding or appreciation or empathy of that, I think that creates a problem too. That you know if... one of my primary concerns is not fully appreciated by my partner, then clearly there is an impact of that on the relationship,” he said, alluding to India-US ties.Jaishankar’s remarks followed US President Donald Trump’s sharing on social media a video clip of Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif’s UNGA speech where he thanked the president for his “timely intervention” to end India’s Op Sindoor. Jaishankar was speaking at the Asia Society Policy Institute where he was asked about the state of the bilateral relationship amid differences over trade and tariffs.The minister said that the trade deal both sides are finalising can improve relations, but added that the period it took to reach the understanding created bumps in the relationship.Bear in mind, India is a society of small producers, small agriculture producers, small factories. Apart from the per capita gap between India and the US, the nature of production, nature of society is very different,” he said.“A trade negotiation required a certain amount of ... patience and detailing to see it through… The expectation that it could rapidly move forward, I think, was tested against a ground reality which was much more complex,” added the minister.Jaishankar said that “today, we have reached a situation where there is more or less an understanding on the trade agreement”.India and the US had in Feb announced the finalisation of the framework for the first phase of the bilateral trade agreement. However, changes in the US tariff landscape have led to further negotiations on the agreement.The two sides have since continued negotiations on their bilateral trade agreement amid the changes in the US tariff regime. Jaishankar, alluding to comments by commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal, said the issue now was what had changed on the American side and how the new Section 301 process would affect the agreement. “The 301 process is still in the works, it’s still unfolding. So the issue for us is at what point do you close out an agreement which is very, very far advanced,” Jaishankar said.“But the period that it took to reach it, that did create bumps last year for the relationship. So presumably, if that agreement is closed out, that would be one point which would contribute to a better relationship,” he said.
Article Summary: S jaishankar: lack of understanding about india’s concerns over cross-border terrorism will affect india-us bilateral ties. India and the us had in feb announced the finalisation of the framework for the first phase of the bilateral trade agreement. Changes in the us tariff landscape have led to further negotiations.

Article Title: Pakistan airspace closed, India eyes China skies
Article Text:
Air India, which lost Rs 4,000 crore due to Pakistan airspace closure in a year, had made a presentation on the Hotan waypoint route.

NEW DELHI: India is trying to work out a “Pakistan bypass” with China for its domestic airlines as the latest closure since April 2025 has made routes between Delhi and West unviable due to longer detours amid soaring oil prices. India is in talks with China to make the Hotan route in Xinjiang available to its airlines.The Hotan plan has been in the works for months, with Air India and IndiGo doing feasibility studies. AI’s Boeing 777s, B787s and Airbus A350s can take the route. IndiGo can do so after it starts getting A350s.“We are exploring alternate airspaces and Hotan is under discussion. Diplomatic-level talks are underway. We are strongly pushing for Hotan. We are asking Indian airlines to launch more international flights from other parts of India (where western routes are not impacted by Pak airspace closure) like the south and improve connectivity from there,” aviation minister Ram Mohan Naidu said on the sidelines of Routes Asia 2027 Tuesday.India is keen on a Pakistan bypass as international travel is growing at about 5% over the past decade, while airlines’ growth plans are hit by the neighbour’s airspace closures.To be sure, India also reciprocally closes its airspace for Pak airlines but their operations are mainly to the West.Air India, which lost Rs 4,000 crore due to Pakistan airspace closure in a year, had made a presentation on the Hotan waypoint route.Some AI wide body aircraft have additional oxygen storage, allowing them more time to step descend to 14,000 feet and then 10,000 feet in case of single engine failure or cabin de-pressurisation while flying out of the region.This is the second time in five years that Air India has found an alternate way around an airspace closure. Before Aug 2021, AI flights used the Pakistan-Afghanistan-Turkmenistan/Uzbekistan route. After Taliban took over Kabul, AI took the longer route via south Pakistan and then Iran-Turkey. In a few months, Air India found a way out by overflying the Hindu Kush.A plane gets lighter as it burns fuel, allowing it to ascend. A wide body taking off from Delhi for Europe or North America is tanked up for the non-stop journey and must overfly the Hindu Kush, where minimum altitude is 30,000 feet. The tallest mountain is 25,289-foot Terich Mir.Air India finalised the Hindu Kush route for the B787 after one-and-a-half months of simulator studies as it could fly at about 35,000 feet. For the heavier B777, it took under four months to finalise procedures for overflying Hindukush and ensure it also maintained 30,000 feet.
Article Summary: India is in talks with china to make the hotan route in xinjiang available to its airlines. Hotan plan has been in the works for months, with air india and indigo doing feasibility studies. Ai’s boeing 777s, b787s and airbus a350s can take the route.

Article Title: 'No locus standi': India rejects Turkey President Erdogan's remarks on Kashmir at UNGA
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Ministry of external affairs on Tuesday slammed Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan for raising the Kashmir issue at the United Nations General Assembly and said that no external party has any locus standi on the issue of India's territorial integrity and sovereignty.During a bi-weekly press briefing, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal rejected Erdogan's remarks and said, “You would have seen that the remarks you referred to were made by the Turkey president. India rejects the unwarranted references to India and the Indian Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir made by the President of Turkey during his address to the UN General Assembly.”“This is a matter, as you would understand, pertaining to India’s territorial integrity and sovereignty, and no external party has any locus standi on this issue,” he added.Earlier on September 22, Erdogan had raised the Kashmir issue at UNGA, saying the matter “should be addressed through dialogue.”“In South Asia, it is important that all disputes, including the Kashmir issue, be addressed through dialogue within the framework of the United Nations Charter and of relevant resolutions,” he said.Turkey has raised the Kashmir issue on global platforms in the past as well.Notably, Erdogan-led Turkey has also formed a Nato-like military alliance with two other Islamic nations, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia.The pact, known as the 'Mecca Pact', was signed between the three countries in August this year.India, however, has consistently rejected any third-party mediation in the Kashmir issue and repeatedly maintained that Jammu and Kashmir is an integral part of India.Following the Pakistan-sponsored terror attack in Pahalgam, India made it clear that New Delhi would only engage with Islamabad on Kashmir-related issues bilaterally.
Article Summary: Turkey has raised the kashmir issue on global platforms in the past as well. Erdogan-led turkey has also formed a nato-like military alliance with two other islamic nations, pakistan and saudi arabia. India, however, has consistently rejected any third-party mediation.

NEW YORK: The ties between India and China are “better” today than they were a couple of years ago, external affairs minister S Jaishankar said, underlining that as border issues are resolved, the relationship returns to normalcy.He was responding to a question on India-China relations, which have seen an upswing in recent times, including President Xi Jinping’s recent visit to India for the Brics Leaders’ Summit hosted by New Delhi.“If you asked me, compared to where you were in 2025, is the relationship better today? He said it was not so much a “structural change”, but part of the reason things had improved was that “they had gone so much off-track that the moment you stabilised it, it was going to improve”.After the 2020 border standoff, the relationship had been impacted, he said.Following the standoff, all “normal contacts” between the two nations had halted, though “trade was continuing”. Official exchanges, visa issuance and flights were impacted. “So once the border standoff was resolved, it was natural that this would start to improve,” he said.

NEW DELHI: The Army on Tuesday killed a Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) terrorist during an encounter in the higher reaches of central Kashmir’s Budgam district, security officials said. The encounter took place in the Korag area of Yousmarg after security forces launched a joint search operation based on specific intelligence inputs.The operation was conducted by the Army, Jammu and Kashmir Police and CRPF Srinagar. The forces were searching the general area of Korag when troops noticed suspicious activity.The troops challenged the suspected terrorists. The terrorists responded by opening fire. Security forces then retaliated, leading to a fierce exchange of gunfire.One terrorist was killed in the exchange. The Army identified him as a member of the banned Lashkar-e-Taiba.The security forces continued their operation in the area after the terrorist was neutralised. Searches were being conducted in the surrounding areas to check for any other terrorists.In a post on X, the Army’s Chinar Corps said, “Based on specific intelligence input, a joint search operation was launched by the Army, J&K Police and CRPF Srinagar in the general area of Korag, Yousmarg.“Vigilant troops observed suspicious activity, and upon being challenged, terrorists opened fire, prompting a fierce exchange of gunfire in which one terrorist was neutralised. Operation is in progress.”The Army did not immediately release further details about the identity of the slain terrorist.It was also not immediately clear whether any weapons or other material had been recovered from the encounter site.The latest operation comes weeks after another terrorist was killed in the same region.Earlier this month, a terrorist identified as Yasir was shot dead in the Yousmarg area. The operation was part of security forces’ efforts to track down terrorists operating in the region.

Article Title: SIR row: At CWC meet, Rahul Gandhi credits Congress for EC 'revelations', gives 'oppose and resist' message

NEW DELHIL Leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Tuesday claimed that Congress's sustained campaign over alleged irregularities in elections had forced differences within the Election Commission over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls into the public domain, news agency PTI reported, citing sources.Speaking at a closed-door meeting of the Congress Working Committee at Indira Bhawan, Rahul Gandhi said revelations about the poll panel were now coming out because of the party's campaign, sources told PTI.He said the Congress had been consistently raising the issue of "vote chori" and highlighting alleged irregularities in the elections in Haryana, Karnataka and Maharashtra, but had initially faced scepticism."The atmosphere has changed over the last two years," Ranhul said, according to PTI sources, attributing the shift largely to the Congress's "fact-based presentations"."The issue is now being discussed in the media and in editorials," he was quoted as saying.During the meeting, Rahul Gandhi said there were two forms of "match-fixing" in elections, one involving electronic voting machines (EVMs) and the other involving alleged deliberate tampering with voter lists."So, there are two forms of match-fixing: EVM match-fixing and voter list match-fixing, both are happening," he reportedly said.The Congress leader also claimed that the 2024 Lok Sabha election was "completely fixed and rigged".He further alleged that legislation enacted thereafter, specifically the law passed in December 2023 providing immunity to the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners, was illegal, sources said.Rahul Gandhi also urged Congress workers not to deviate from the path of "virodh" (opposition) and "pratirodh" (resistance), from the streets to Parliament, according to PTI sources.Invoking the Lahore Congress session of 1929, Gandhi said the party had chosen the path of "Purna Swaraj" at a time when the British government had denied Congress even provincial autonomy.As the present government refuses to listen to the voice of the people of this country or heed their demands, there is only one way forward for parties that believe in democracy -- to resist, sources quoted him as saying.The comes as Congress demanded the immediate removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, suspension of the SIR, restoration of over 13 crore names struck off from the electoral rolls and the resignation of Prime Minister Narendra Modi for "match-fixing" polls.The meeting comes days after The Indian Express reported that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised objections on record at least 14 times in the past 10 months over SIR decisions and orders they said were issued without their knowledge or recommendation.Amid questions over the objections raised by the two commissioners, the EC has maintained that differing views and observations are a normal part of deliberations in any institution. It has also asserted that all its orders carry full legal sanction and follow established statutory procedures.
Article Summary: Rahul gandhi claims congress's sustained campaign over alleged irregularities in elections has forced differences within the election commission into the public domain. He said revelations about the poll panel were now coming out because of the party's campaign. Gandhi also claimed that the 2024 lok sabha election was "completely fixed and rigged"

Article Title: GSK India sets Guinness World Records title with giant brochure mosaic on World Heart Day
Article Text:
GSK India’s 115-square-metre brochure mosaic and Guinness World Records certificate recognising it as the 'largest brochure mosaic-image'

GSK India has received a Guinness World Records title for the “largest brochure mosaic-image”, with a 115-square-metre installation assembled from pledge-card brochures contributed by more than 5,000 healthcare professionals.The mosaic was created at GSK House in Mumbai as part of an awareness initiative around adult immunisation and preventive healthcare, coinciding with World Heart Day.The company said the initiative focused on raising awareness about adult vaccination among older adults and people with underlying cardiovascular conditions.According to the release, adult immunisation coverage in India remains below 2%, citing a Journal of the Association of Physicians of India (JAPI) paper.GSK said the campaign also sought to highlight the risk of shingles and its complications among older adults with cardiovascular diseases.

A decade later: What changed?

NEW DELHI: Ten years ago, on the night of September 28-29, 2016, Indian Army commandos crossed the Line of Control and carried out surgical strikes on terrorist launch pads in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir.The operation, carried out in response to the Pakistan-sponsored Uri terror attack, marked a hard-hitting response to Pakistan for sheltering and cultivating terror on its soil.It was the first time India responded not with a traditional full-fledged war, but with a calibrated and deliberate military operation against Islamabad-backed terror infrastructure across the border.It was also a demonstration of the more assertive counter-terrorism approach that the Modi government would later associate with its “New India” and “zero tolerance” messaging.But the story of the surgical strikes did not begin on the night of September 28.It began 10 days earlier, in a burning Army camp in Uri.At around 5.30am on September 18, four heavily armed terrorists attacked the Army's 12th Brigade headquarters in Jammu and Kashmir's Uri, close to the Line of Control.The attack was on a rear administrative camp next to the brigade headquarters.The timing was particularly devastating. Troops were in the middle of a changeover, with an advance party of the incoming 6 Bihar unit in the process of replacing the outgoing 10 Dogra unit.Many soldiers were housed in temporary tents. Explosions and gunfire triggered a fire that spread through the camp.Seventeen soldiers were killed in the initial attack. Two others later succumbed to their injuries, taking the toll to 19.The four attackers were killed then and there.For the families, however, the numbers told only part of the story.In Rajasthan, Havaldar Nimb Singh Rawat's family was preparing to receive his body on what would have been his 48th birthday. A member of 6 Bihar, Rawat had routinely spent his birthdays on duty because his family lived away in Rajsamand district. He left behind his wife, four daughters and a young son.In Samba, 10-year-old Vansh, the son of Havildar Ravi Paul Salotra of 10 Dogra, said he wanted to fulfil his father's dream of becoming an Army doctor.The attack had suddenly turned a distant security crisis into funerals, grieving families and children asking questions.Prime Minister Narendra Modi's first response came within hours.“We strongly condemn the cowardly terror attack in Uri. I assure the nation that those behind this despicable attack will not go unpunished,” PM Modi said.He also said the country saluted those martyred and that their service would always be remembered.The government began examining the attack, including the identity and possible origins of the attackers.Then-home minister Rajnath Singh cancelled a planned visit to Russia and the US and convened a security review in Delhi.“Pakistan is a terrorist state and it should be identified and isolated as such,” Rajnath Singh said on September 18, adding that there were indications that the attackers were highly trained, heavily armed and specially equipped.However, the public anger and government's rhetoric did not immediately translate into military strike.Within 24 hours, the government had begun examining possible responses.National security adviser Ajit Doval chaired a meeting of senior intelligence and military officials, according to contemporary reports, with options being prepared for the Prime Minister.One line attributed to the discussions captured the government's thinking: India would avenge the deaths, but “at a time of our choosing”.Outside the government, the demand for retaliation was growing.BJP general secretary Ram Madhav wrote on Facebook: “For one tooth, the complete jaw.”The expression reflected the anger after Uri. But inside the security establishment, the calculations were more complicated.Pakistan had heightened its alert along the LoC and an immediate strike risked escalation.This was the first crucial decision of the 10-day story.India would respond.But it would decide when, where and how.The government began weighing its choices.Diplomatic pressure was one part of the response. Within hours of the Uri attack, Indian missions abroad were asked to mobilise international condemnation of the attack.Then-external affairs mnister Sushma Swaraj would subsequently use the UN platform to attack Pakistan's support for terrorism.But the military option was also being examined.The Army was already monitoring terrorist infrastructure across the LoC. The DGMO would later say that almost 20 infiltration attempts had been foiled by the Army at or close to the LoC during 2016. India had also recovered GPS devices and other material that it said pointed to Pakistan as the source of the infiltration network.The question was no longer simply whether India could strike.It was whether it could strike in a way that was precise, limited and militarily useful.By the third week of September, the military option was becoming more concrete.The targets were terrorist launch pads close to the LoC, where India believed militants were preparing to infiltrate Jammu and Kashmir.The proposed operation was not conceived as a conventional attack on Pakistan.The intended targets were terrorist infrastructure. The troops would cross the LoC, strike the launch pads and withdraw.The political leadership had to weigh the possibility that Pakistan would retaliate. The military had to work out routes, timings, surveillance and extraction.It was a narrow window between sending a message and triggering something much bigger. There was also a risk of indulging in a war with nuclear-armed neighbour.On September 24, PM Narendra Modi met the chiefs of the Army and Air Force and the vice chief of the Navy, with NSA Ajit Doval also present, as discussions focused on the security situation and India’s response to the Uri attack.Later that day, speaking at a BJP rally in Kerala's Kozhikode, he addressed the families of the soldiers killed in Uri.PM warned that those responsible would be held accountable.The signal was becoming unmistakable. But the military operation remained secret.That evening, there was still no public indication that Indian Special Forces were preparing to cross the LoC.The next few days were quieter in public, but crucial behind the scenes.According to Manohar Parrikar Institute under defence ministry, the Special Forces contingent selected for the operation was divided into smaller groups and moved towards the LoC, close to the Army’s forward positions. Later accounts of the operation said the teams moved after last light, crossed gaps in their own minefields and began closing in on the identified targets.The terrain itself was a challenge. The minefields ahead of Indian defences remained a constant danger, with mines sometimes shifting because of heavy rains and landslides. As the teams moved closer, the target areas were kept under watch for any changes that could affect the mission.At the designated hour, the teams struck.They then began their withdrawal, moving back towards their positions before daybreak.For the soldiers preparing to cross the LoC, this was no longer about speeches in Delhi.It was about moving through difficult terrain in darkness, reaching the targets, completing the mission and making it back safely.The Army would later say the operation was based on “very credible and specific information” about terrorist teams positioned at launch pads along the LoC and preparing to infiltrate and carry out attacks.The political leadership, meanwhile, kept the circle of people aware of the operation tightly controlled.As darkness fell on September 28, the operation entered its final phase.Special Forces teams moved towards their designated targets.In the early hours of September 29, they crossed the Line of Control and entered the areas under Pakistan's illegal occupation where the Army had identified terrorist launch pads.The Army later said the teams struck several launch pads across multiple sectors along the LoC. After completing their mission, they began withdrawing before dawn.The operation was over.Then came the second, equally important decision. India would tell the world what it had done.The announcement came that morning.Then-DGMO Lt Gen Ranbir Singh appeared before the media and said the Army had conducted “surgical strikes” at several launch pads.The decision, he said, followed “very credible and specific information” that terrorist teams had positioned themselves at launch pads along the LoC with the aim of infiltrating Jammu and Kashmir and carrying out terrorist strikes in India.The Army said the strikes had caused “significant casualties” to terrorists and those supporting them.Singh also made clear that the operation had ended, saying there were no plans for further continuation of the strikes.India was not merely signalling that it had retaliated. It was publicly acknowledging that its forces had crossed the LoC and struck what it described as terrorist launch pads.Pakistan rejected India's account of a surgical strike and said its soldiers had come under fire.For the Union government, however, the operation had acquired a significance beyond the battlefield.It had chosen to publicly own the operation and put its account of the events on record.Cross-LoC raids were not unprecedented.Indian troops had conducted tactical operations across the LoC before. What changed in 2016 was the combination of political authorisation, the scale of the operation and, above all, the decision to publicly acknowledge it.The government did not leave the operation as an unconfirmed military action.The then-DGMO briefed the country.The term “surgical strikes” entered India's national-security vocabulary.And the PM Modi-led government presented the operation as a calibrated response to terrorism, rather than the opening move in a conventional war.That distinction was crucial.India had chosen to hit terrorist infrastructure without declaring war on Pakistan.However, the September 2016 strikes did not end Pakistan-manufactured terrorism.In February 2019, a Jaish-e-Mohammed suicide bomber attacked a CRPF convoy in Pulwama, killing 40 personnel.Twelve days later, on February 26, the Indian Air Force carried out an air strike on a Jaish-e-Mohammed facility at Balakot in mainland Pakistan.The response had now moved beyond the LoC as Balakot is close to international border and situated in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province.India had demonstrated that air power, too, could be used against terrorist infrastructure across the border.The 2016 template had evolved.In 2025, the response was broader still.Following the April 22 Pahalgam terror attack, which killed 26 people, India launched Operation Sindoor on May 7.The government said the armed forces struck nine terrorist infrastructure sites in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir. It described the initial strikes as "focused and measured".The strikes were not limited to terrorist infrastructure. After Pakistan launched waves of drones and missiles towards Indian territory, New Delhi expanded its response to include military targets.India then struck Pakistani military installations, targeting 11 airbases as part of the broader operation.The confrontation subsequently expanded, involving missiles, drones, air-defence systems and attacks on military targets before the Pakistani side pleaded India for a ceasefire on land, air and water.On Pakistan DGMO's request, India announced ceasefire on May 10.The technology and scale were vastly different from 2016.But the sequence was familiar.The Army's counterterrorism architecture has now evolved.The response now relies heavily on intelligence-led operations, surveillance, drones, satellite imagery, counter-infiltration measures and precision weapons.A decade later, the battlefield is increasingly shaped by sensors, drones, precision weapons and real-time intelligence.
Article Summary: Ten years ago, indian army commandos carried out surgical strikes on terrorist launch pads in pakistan-occupied kashmir. Operation marked a hard-hitting response to pakistan for sheltering and cultivating terror on its soil. It was the first time india responded not with a traditional full-fledged war, but with a calibrated and deliberate military operation.

Article Title: 'Is Congress giving clean chit to EC in Kerala, Punjab, Himachal?' BJP's Smriti Irani on SIR row
Article Text:
Smriti Irani defends the Election Commission amid Congress’ SIR demands, questioning its objection to duplicate and deceased names on electoral rolls

NEW DELHI: BJP national general secretary Smriti Z Irani on Tuesday defended the Election Commission amid Congress’ demands for the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and suspension of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), questioning the opposition party's objections to duplicate and deceased names appearing on electoral rolls.She questioned whether Congress was raising similar concerns about the EC in states such as Himachal Pradesh, Punjab, Kerala and Karnataka, where the BJP is not in power. She also said the Election Commission strengthens India's democratic framework and accused Congress of targeting the poll panel instead of introspecting over its electoral defeats."The question arises: In states like Himachal Pradesh, Punjab, Kerala, and Karnataka, where the Bharatiya Janata Party is not in power, is the Congress leadership giving the Election Commission a clean chit, or is it questioning the Commission's activities there as well?" she said."If a name appears as a duplicate on the electoral roll, or if the name of a deceased person appears on the electoral roll, why does the Congress Party want it restored? Why does the Congress Party want duplicate names to remain on the electoral roll?... Why does the Congress Party want to ensure that duplicate names persist on the electoral rolls?..." Irani added.Irani also hit out at Congress over its reference to the Lahore Congress Session, bringing up the historical role of A.O.Hume."I am astonished that today the Congress leadership cited the Lahore Congress Session. Since the Congress Party wishes to turn the pages of history, it should also turn to the page that reveals the party's origins to the people of the country, specifically, how AO Hume, who served as Secretary for Revenue, Agriculture, and Commerce under the British Empire, shared a suggestion with the Viceroy that a political organization, the Congress Party, should be formed to safeguard the British Empire. The very Congress Party that was established to protect the British Empire is today attacking the Election Commission of India by citing the Lahore Congress Session. There could be nothing more shameful than this," she said.The remarks came after the Congress Working Committee demanded the immediate removal of Kumar, suspension of the SIR and restoration of 13.30 crore names it claimed had been removed from electoral rolls. The party also demanded Prime Minister Narendra Modi's resignation, alleging "match-fixing" between the Election Commission and the BJP-led government.Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh said Rahul Gandhi had raised concerns about elections in Haryana, Karnataka and Maharashtra, claiming that subsequent developments had vindicated those concerns."The elections in our country are not fair and transparent. They are match-fixing elections - match fixing between the Election Commission and PM-HM duo," Ramesh said.The CWC resolution alleged that the SIR process raised serious concerns over the integrity and transparency of electoral rolls and demanded its immediate suspension. It also said the party would resist the issue in Parliament, courts and on the streets.The Congress' demands came days after The Indian Express reported that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had recorded objections at least 14 times over 10 months to decisions and orders concerning the SIR process.The EC has maintained that differing views and observations are a normal part of institutional deliberations and that its orders carry full legal sanction and follow established statutory procedures.
Article Summary: Smriti irani defends the election commission amid congress’ sir demands, questioning its objection to duplicate and deceased names on electoral rolls. She also accused congress of targeting the poll panel instead of introspecting over its electoral defeats.

Article Title: ‘Beating his drum away’: Congress targets PM Modi for ‘ignoring’ rising inflation in Mann Ki Baat
Article Text:
Cong targets PM Modi for 'ignoring' inflation

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

(With ANI inputs)

NEW DELHI: The Congress on Monday questioned Prime Minister Narendra Modi for not addressing rising inflation in his Mann Ki Baat radio address, accusing him of being “blissfully unconcerned” about the issue.The opposition party’s attack came a day after PM Modi addressed the nation in the 138th episode of Mann Ki Baat.“The brunt of inflation is no longer confined just to the kitchen, yet the Prime Minister remains blissfully unconcerned, beating his drum away. Vegetables are getting more expensive by the day, with onion prices soaring 48.27% in August. Items such as air conditioners, TVs and refrigerators are also set to become more expensive. Household savings are steadily declining, while family debt is mounting. In such a scenario, how is the common family supposed to meet its needs?” Congress MP Jairam Ramesh wrote on X.Ramesh questioned why PM Modi continues to “sermonise” in the Mann Ki Baat series instead of addressing the public’s concerns.“In his ‘Mann Ki Baat’ radio series, the Prime Minister keeps sermonising on various issues, but when will he address the country’s most pressing concern—inflation? When will he care about the public’s worries? The public is already beleaguered by rising prices, and there’s no relief coming from the government.How on earth is the average family supposed to manage its budget? How long will the middle class and the poor have their backs broken like this?” the Rajya Sabha MP asked.According to the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation’s (MoSPI) Consumer Price Index (CPI) release, retail inflation, based on the 2024=100 CPI, stood at 4.82% in August, up from 4.45% in July. Food inflation, measured by the Consumer Food Price Index (CFPI), rose to 5.95% in August from 5.52% in July. The August figures are provisional.Official data showed that onion inflation surged from 22.54% in July to 48.27% in August. Ginger recorded inflation of 73.82%, while garlic inflation stood at 43.60%. In contrast, tomato prices fell 31.09% year-on-year, while potato prices declined 13.14%.MoSPI data showed inflation in the combined food and beverages category at 5.66% in August. Transport inflation stood at 4.60 percent, education services at 3.73%, while restaurants and accommodation services recorded inflation of 8.38%. Personal care, social protection and miscellaneous goods and services registered inflation of 15.17%.The CPI data was compiled from price information collected across 1,407 urban markets, including online markets, and 1,465 villages nationwide. MoSPI reported a 100% response rate from both rural and urban markets in August.According to MoSPI, the next CPI data, covering September, is scheduled to be released on October 12.
Article Summary: Cong targets pm modi for 'ignoring' inflation in his mann ki baat radio address. Opposition party’s attack came a day after pm modi addressed the nation. Food inflation, measured by the consumer food price index (cfpi), rose to 5.95% in august.

Article Title: Hijacking scare on Dubai-Tel Aviv flight; emergency code triggered, plane diverted to Saudi Arabia
Article Text:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu held consultations with security officials after the flight was diverted

Netanyahu, military officials hold consultations

A Flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv carrying around 180 people landed at Tabuk airport in Saudi Arabia on Wednesday after transmitting emergency signals that triggered a reported hijack scare.The aircraft initially transmitted squawk code 7700, the international transponder code for a general emergency, before sending code 7500, which indicates hijacking or unlawful interference, according to flight-tracking data cited by The Times of Israel. The aircraft subsequently turned around while flying over Saudi Arabia and was diverted to Tabuk, where it landed safely.The incident that prompted the emergency signals was apparently an altercation between the pilots aboard the aircraft, according to Israeli security sources cited by The Times of Israel. The report said a hijacking was subsequently ruled out.The 7500 signal prompted Israeli Air Force fighter jets to scramble towards the aircraft, according to Israeli security sources cited by the publication. The aircraft also briefly disappeared from flight-tracking websites after transmitting the emergency signals, adding to the uncertainty surrounding the incident.Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu held consultations with security officials after the flight was diverted, three Israeli security officials told Reuters.An Israeli source had earlier said the situation would become clearer once the aircraft landed in Saudi Arabia.The Israel Defence Forces also held an assessment of the incident. IDF Chief of Staff Lt Gen Eyal Zamir met senior officers including Israeli Air Force chief Maj Gen Omer Tischler, Operations Directorate chief Maj Gen Itzik Cohen and Intelligence Directorate chief Maj Gen Shlomi Binder, The Times of Israel reported.
Article Summary: Flydubai flight from dubai to tel aviv landed at tabuk airport in saudi arabia. The aircraft initially transmitted squawk code 7700, the international transponder code for a general emergency. It then sent code 7500, which indicates hijacking or unlawful interference.

Article Title: "Made him a target for verbal attack and physical threats": Candace Owens sued by Utah man over alleged Charlie Kirk shooting accusations
Article Text:
Candace Owens (Image via Getty)

Utah man details alleged fallout from Candace Owens claims

Charlie Kirk shooting claims allegedly led to threats

A Utah man who says he was simply attending Charlie Kirk’s 2026 rally has filed a lawsuit against political commentator Candace Owens, alleging that her podcast coverage falsely tied him to Kirk’s killing. Robert Hild Jr. claims the accusations turned his life upside down, damaged his reputation and exposed his family to unwanted attention and threats. The lawsuit, filed Monday, also details how social media posts and photographs were allegedly used to support claims against him. Hild says he has repeatedly sought a retraction, but the disputed statements continued to circulate among Owens’ audience.Hild was present at the Utah Valley University event on Sept. 10, 2026, when Kirk was fatally shot. According to the lawsuit, he witnessed the attack and later took shelter at the home of his friend’s grandmother with others who had been at the rally.The case says the situation changed after photographs emerged showing alleged shooter Tyler Robinson near the home where Hild and his companions had stayed. The FBI later released a separate image of Robinson inside a stairwell on the UVU campus.Hild argues that those circumstances were misinterpreted. The lawsuit says he, his friend and a roommate later walked along a trail Robinson was believed to have taken and took selfies. A friend subsequently shared those images online.According to Hild, Owens used those social media photographs during her podcast coverage and suggested that he had a connection to the suspect. The lawsuit says she also alleged that Hild had ties to foreign actors and a Ukrainian military group with alleged links to neo-Nazis.The lawsuit says Hild attempted to persuade Owens to correct or withdraw the allegations, but claims she declined. It further alleges that Owens continued discussing him despite people providing information about his presence at the rally.The fallout, Hild says, went beyond online criticism. He claims followers shared personal information about him and members of his family, including names and home addresses. The lawsuit also alleges that his home and vehicle were vandalized.Hild says the situation became serious enough that law enforcement advised him and his roommates not to remain at their home.In the lawsuit, Hild describes himself as a "private citizen who was in the process of building a happy and productive life far from the public spotlight." He also says he "experienced the trauma of watching a horrific murder up close."The legal complaint alleges that the claims have "upended his life, irreparably damaged his reputation, and made him a target for verbal attack and physical threats."The allegations in the lawsuit remain claims at this stage. The filing now places the dispute over Owens’ statements and their alleged consequences before the court.
Article Summary: Robert hild jr. claims the accusations turned his life upside down, damaged his reputation and exposed his family to unwanted attention and threats. Hild says he has repeatedly sought a retraction, but the disputed statements continued to circulate among owens’ audience.

Article Title: Oil stays above $103 after Trump denies easing sanctions on Iran
Article Text:
Oil prices inch higher

Qatar seeks common ground

Middle East supply picks up

Oil prices inched higher on Wednesday, trading beyond the $103 per barrel mark as uncertainty over the US stance towards Iran returned to the spotlight. US The momentum came after US President Donald Trump rejected a report that Washington was prepared to ease sanctions on Tehran. Qatar, meanwhile, said it was continuing efforts to bring Iran and the US towards an agreement.Brent crude rose 0.56% to $103.20, while WTI crude gained 0.11% to $89.48. The gains came a day after oil prices declined as crude supplies from the Middle East showed signs of recovering.As the Strait of Hormuz remains choked for a seventh month, oil prices have continued to rise. Brent is set to gain around 14% in September, which would be its biggest monthly increase since July. WTI is headed for a rise of about 4% after crossing $106 for the first time since May.The gap between Brent and WTI has also widened to its highest level in four months this month. Traders have been assessing possible US restrictions on diesel exports, which could result in an oversupply in the domestic market and reduce the amount of crude processed by US refiners.Trump is considering allowing sales of red-dyed diesel instead of imposing an export ban, according to Reuters.The move would be aimed at offering some relief to consumers as the November mid-term elections approach.Qatar on Tuesday said that it hoped its shuttle diplomacy between Iran and the US could help the two sides reach a breakthrough."We are exchanging messages between the parties, and we're working towards establishing a common ground in order to get into a deal that would save all of us from the repercussions of the conflict," Qatar's foreign ministry spokesperson Majed al-Ansari said.The diplomatic efforts came amid a report by Axios that cited US officials as saying Trump was willing to offer Iran sanctions relief and release frozen Iranian funds in return for "concrete" steps by Tehran on its nuclear programme.Trump rejected the report, saying "This is untrue. I offered them NOTHING."The recovery in regional oil flows has also emerged as a key factor for the market. Saudi Arabia resumed oil tanker loadings from its Red Sea port of Yanbu on Tuesday after restarting operations on the East-West Pipeline.Oil exports from Middle Eastern producers rose to 16.328 million barrels per day in September, their highest level since the US-Israeli war with Iran began in late February.US inventory figures also remained in focus. Crude oil and gasoline stocks increased last week, while distillate inventories declined, according to market sources citing data from the American Petroleum Institute.US crude inventories rose by 1.02 million barrels in the week ended September 25, the sources said.The official US Energy Information Administration inventory data is due at 10:30 a.m. EDT (1430 GMT). Analysts polled by Reuters expect crude and product inventories to have declined.
Article Summary: Brent crude rose 0.56% to $103.20, while wti crude gained 0.11%. The momentum came after us president donald trump rejected a report that washington was prepared to ease sanctions on tehran. Qatar, meanwhile, said it was continuing efforts to bring iran and the us towards an agreement.

Article Title: Trump embraces Xi as peer, alarms partners and critics
Article Text: TOI correspondent from Washington: A 48-hour state visit to the United States by China’s President Xi Jinping yielded no immediate major breakthroughs but confirmed the broad impression, in visuals and much as words, that Washington now accepts China as a peer in a new G-2 formulation.For all the talk of trade, artificial intelligence, Taiwan, Iran and strategic competition, the most consequential message of Xi’s visit may have been the choreography itself. A fawning Trump repeatedly described Xi as a friend and the relationship as a “great friendship,” with little personal reciprocity from the Chinese leader.The charitable explanation for what many critics said was Trump’s folding before Xi and muting his demands from and tirades against China was purportedly in the service of American farmers – his major voting bloc – who are getting screwed because Beijing cut down purchase of soy, corn, and other farm produce. In brief remarks during a tea ceremony, the MAGA supremo mentioned that the visit had yielded “great results” for American farmers without elaborating, but spoke of little else other than accepting Xi’s invitation to visit China.By most accounts, the summit produced a lot of optics, but little else, amid a cascade of criticism that Trump is placating China rather than confronting it over its actions inimical to US, including its tacit support for Iran.The most withering censure came from Republican Senator John Kennedy of Louisiana, who likened Xi and leaders of Russia, North Korea and Iran, to reptiles. "The chief reptile, the quarterback, is President Xi. They all lie like timeshare salesmen. You can’t trust them. I wouldn’t turn my back on any of them, even if I thought and knew they were two days dead,” Kennedy told a TV show during the visit. Even Senator Chuck Grassley, the Iowa Republican whose state is deeply dependent on agricultural exports, was sceptical about the outcome of the visit, saying that if extending the trade truce was all that emerged, the summit risked becoming a “show job" for a communist autocrat.On Taiwan, the most sensitive strategic issue between the two sides, there was no public breakthrough. Trump has continued to hold in abeyance a roughly $14 billion Taiwan weapons package that he described earlier this year as a negotiating chip with Beijing. China wants the arms sales halted; US lawmakers across party lines have urged their release.Nor were there any signs of a significant Chinese concession on Iran. Beijing has expressed interest in peace and stability but remains economically intertwined with Tehran. On advanced chips, Washington also appeared to hold its line, despite Beijing’s interest in easing US technology restrictions. That may ultimately prove more consequential than the ceremonial theatrics. The summit thus produced no obvious quid pro quo in which China would use its leverage over Iran in return for a major American concession.Trump’s defenders argued though that the president’s approach should be judged against what they described as decades of failed China policy under previous administrations. “Obama and Biden talked tough, but gave away American factories to the Chinese. Trump actually launched a trade war against China,” noted Brian Kilmeade on Fox News, pointing out that Trump "kicked the Chinese out of Panama Canal" and went after their “favourite oil proxies in our hemisphere, Venezuela and Iran, and is about to kick them out of Cuba. ”That in essence is the larger contradiction of the summit. Trump has not abandoned confrontation with China; he has instead recast it as transactional management between two superpowers, much to the consternation of other nations like India, Japan, and South Korea. Xi, for his part, repeatedly spoke not of friendship between two men but of China and the US as “two major countries” with a responsibility to find a new way of coexisting.The symbolism was perhaps captured most neatly by the contrasting tours offered during the two leaders’ encounters. When Trump visited Beijing in May, Xi showed him ancient trees at Zhongnanhai, including specimens more than 1,000 years old — a quiet display of Chinese historical depth and long-term continuity. In Washington, Trump showed Xi his new White House helipad, built in a “record” 12 weeks – which the Chinese would have built in 12 days if not 12 hours.
Article Summary: Xi jinping's 48-hour state visit to the united states yielded no immediate major breakthroughs. But it confirmed the broad impression, in visuals and much as words, that washington now accepts china as a peer in a new g-2 formulation.

Article Title: ‘No Muslim can even dare’: Pakistan PM at UN condemns Houthi attacks, draws red line over Mecca
Article Text:
Pakistan's PM Shehbaz Sharif speaks at UNGA

NEW DELHI: Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday used the 81st United Nations General Assembly to condemn Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and warn against any threat to the safety and sanctity of Mecca.He also defended Pakistan’s new defence pact with Saudi Arabia and Türkiye, while highlighting Islamabad’s diplomatic efforts to bring the United States and Iran to the negotiating table."We once again condemn, in the strongest possible terms, the recent deplorable attacks by the Houthis against the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia," Sharif said in his address."The attempted drone attack on the holy city of Mecca al-Mukarramah has outraged Muslims across the globe. Any threat to safety and sanctity... is a red line that must never be crossed. No Muslim can even dare to think of committing such a heinous (act)."Saudi Arabia has accused the Houthis of targeting Mecca with a drone, an allegation the Houthis denied. Riyadh has also reported intercepting Houthi ballistic missiles following renewed hostilities in the region.Sharif also sought to underline Islamabad’s diplomatic role in the conflict between the United States and Iran, saying Pakistan had worked to bring the two sides to the negotiating table.“Pakistan chose to act swiftly through concerted efforts. Pakistan successfully brought Washington and Tehran under one roof in Islamabad. From the Islamabad talks to the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding, many historic steps were taken to bring an end to this serious conflict,” he said.The Pakistani prime minister also referred to the recently signed defence agreement between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Türkiye. The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement provides for collective defence commitments among the three countries, while Pakistani officials have said the arrangement is not directed against any particular state.Sharif said the pact was intended to serve defence, stability and peace rather than confrontation.On Palestine, Sharif denounced what he called Israel’s “genocidal agenda” and condemned what he described as “Israeli aggression against Lebanon and Syria”.He also thanked Pakistan’s Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff, Field Marshal Asim Munir, crediting his “relentless efforts” with helping create “space for diplomacy under exceptionally difficult and challenging circumstances”.Sharif further thanked US President Donald Trump for what he called his “timely intervention” during the 2025 India-Pakistan conflict, saying it had “saved hundreds of millions of lives in South Asia”.His remarks came as Pakistan balances its ties with Iran with its deepening strategic and defence relationship with Saudi Arabia, while regional tensions continue to test Islamabad’s stated preference for diplomacy.
Article Summary: Pakistan's pm shehbaz sharif condemns houthi attacks on saudi arabia. Warns against any threat to the safety and sanctity of mecca. Defends pakistan's new defence pact with saudi arabia and türkiye. Underlines islamabad's diplomatic efforts to bring u.s. and iran to negotiating table.

Article Title: US government’s new order replaces ‘artificial intelligence’ with ‘Super Intelligence’; federal agencies directed to use new term
Article Text:
US President Donald Trump signs executive order directing federal agencies to stop using “artificial intelligence” and instead use the term “Super Intelligence”

Why is Trump calling AI ‘ Super Intelligence ’

‘Super intelligence’ already has a different meaning in AI

Trump has been using the term for days

What does the name change mean for users

US President Donald Trump has signed an executive order directing federal agencies to stop using “artificial intelligence” and instead use the term “Super Intelligence”, or “SI”, in their official communications. The move comes as the Trump administration continues to push for rapid AI development while concerns grow over AI safety, job losses and autonomous systems acting without direct human control. The order says the new term better reflects what advanced AI systems can do and the opportunities they could create. Trump had already started using “Super Intelligence” in public remarks, including at the United Nations last week.The executive order says the technology has moved beyond simply copying or automating individual parts of human intelligence. “As these capabilities continue to improve, they increasingly represent not merely artificial intelligence, but a new era of Super Intelligence,” the order said. “It’s not artificial, we all agree on that,” Trump told reporters on Tuesday.The order directs federal agencies to use “Super Intelligence” or “SI” when referring to the technology in public communications, websites, reports, policy documents and other official material.It also gives Michael Kratsios, director of the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy, responsibility for deciding whether the government's definition of the term should be changed or expanded. “Within 60 days of the date of this order, the Assistant to the President for Science and Technology (APST), in consultation with the heads of other agencies as the APST deems appropriate, shall submit to the President proposed legislative language to establish a Federal definition of “Super Intelligence” and “SI” that reflects the capabilities described in section 1 of this order,” the order stated.The term is not new to the AI industry. In AI research, superintelligence generally refers to a system that is more capable than humans across virtually all areas of cognitive work. Such a system has not been achieved.Trump's executive order uses the term more broadly for the rapidly developing AI technology being built today.This makes the change more than a simple wording update. Federal agencies will now be expected to use the administration's preferred terminology when discussing AI in their public-facing work.Trump began using “Super Intelligence” publicly before signing the executive order. During his address to the United Nations last week, he said the US would reject attempts to create a global system for controlling AI and referred to the technology as “Super Intelligence.”The White House has also used the term in its recent policy announcements. Following Trump's meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping, the two countries agreed to use “super intelligence” rather than “artificial intelligence” for the emerging technology. They also agreed to create a US-China Super Intelligence Dialogue to discuss its risks and benefits.The change in terminology comes as the debate over AI safety is becoming more intense. Trump has repeatedly argued that the US needs to remain ahead in AI development, particularly as it competes with China. His administration has also favoured working with AI companies rather than imposing broad new regulations.For most people, the immediate impact is likely to be limited. The executive order changes the terminology used by federal agencies rather than creating a new type of AI technology.Government websites, reports and policy documents will increasingly refer to “Super Intelligence” or “SI” instead of “artificial intelligence.” The administration says “Super Intelligence” better captures the rapid development and potential of AI. At the same time, AI companies and policymakers continue to debate how to prevent powerful systems from being misused or acting outside their intended purpose.
Article Summary: Us president donald trump signs executive order directing federal agencies to stop using ‘artificial intelligence’ and instead use the term ‘super intelligence’ the order says the new term better reflects what advanced ai systems can do and the opportunities they could create.
